newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Skulking under weak rand, S.African shrs end down.
newsitem.headline: Skulking under weak rand, S.African shrs end down.

text.p: South African shares spent the day skulking beneath the shadow of a dismal rand and gilts market, finishing weaker but off their day's worst.

"Industrials and all-shares were mostly affected by the rand. Still, they didn't fall as far as they might have which means investors might have found some attraction in equities today," one dealer said.
Dealers said further equity courage could have come from the fact that the currency market was rather thin and so volatility was exaggerated.
Foreigners were the ones most spooked by any fall in the rand, they said.
With Wall Street already looking weak, dealers said the softer trend was likely to persist for a while, although they cautioned that no panic was likely to set in.
Wall Street was last 27.95 points weaker at 6,008.51.
Buoyed by the firmer bullion price for much of the day, gold shares nosed above opening levels at one stage but, as the metal softened, shares lost confidence and dropped.
The market was seen remaining cautious ahead of Friday's September preliminary M3 money supply and trade data.
The overall index was off 20 points to 7,016.4, industrials lost 7.0 points to 8,274.4 and golds were off 14.1 points to 1,713.7 points.
